title: More Verbs
description: The verbs of real conversation in their full me- and ber- forms, the way you'd say them politely, with the shorter root that casual speech uses: helping, deciding, borrowing, meeting up, picking someone up.

items.registerNotes: Casually bantu, or bantuin in Jakarta-style speech. Shop staff greet you with Ada yang bisa saya bantu? (Can I help you?).
Built on arti (meaning), in its old form erti. Casually ngerti: Ngerti nggak? Paham means the same and is just as common.
items.pitfallNote: A flat Saya tidak mengerti can sound blunt; Maaf, saya kurang mengerti (Sorry, I don't quite follow) is the gentle way to say it.

items.registerNotes: From jelas (clear): to make clear. Politely, Bisa dijelaskan lagi? (Could you explain that again?); casually, jelasin.
Casually mutusin, which also means to break up with someone: Dia mutusin pacarnya.
items.pitfallNote: The root putus on its own means broken off or split up (Kami sudah putus, We've broken up), so for deciding use the full memutuskan.

items.english: to prepare, to get something ready
items.registerNotes: From siap (ready). Casually siapin: Aku siapin makan dulu, ya (I'll get the food ready first).
The terima of terima kasih (thank you). Casually just terima: Udah terima uangnya? (Have you got the money?)
Casually pinjam. To lend is meminjamkan, casually pinjamin.
items.pitfallNote: To ask someone to lend you something, ask to borrow it: Boleh saya pinjam payungnya? (Could I borrow your umbrella?), rather than translating 'lend me'.

items.registerNotes: From kembali (to come back): to bring something back. Casually balikin: Besok aku balikin, ya (I'll give it back tomorrow).
Casually ketemu: Ketemu di mana? (Where shall we meet?). You meet dengan someone: bertemu dengan teman.

items.english: to set off, to leave (on a journey)
items.registerNotes: The same in casual speech: Jam berapa berangkat? Friends also say jalan for setting off: Yuk, jalan.
items.pitfallNote: It's the leaving, not the going: Saya berangkat jam tujuh means you set off at seven. Arriving is sampai or tiba.

items.registerNotes: For giving something up as well as for vehicles: berhenti merokok (to quit smoking), berhenti kerja (to quit a job). To a driver, casually: Stop di sini, Pak.

items.english: to get married, to be married
items.registerNotes: Casually nikah: Kapan nikah? (When are you getting married?)
items.pitfallNote: Sudah menikah? (Are you married?) is answered Sudah or Belum (not yet), not Tidak. Belum is the normal reply for anyone single.
items.cultureNote: Marriage and children are ordinary small talk, even with people you've just met. A light Belum, doakan saja, ya (Not yet, keep me in your prayers) answers it gracefully.

items.registerNotes: Casually pakai, often said pake: Pakai helm, ya. Paying by card is bayar pakai kartu.
items.pitfallNote: One word for both wearing and using: pakai baju (wear clothes), pakai sendok (use a spoon).

items.english: to try; to try on, to taste
items.registerNotes: Casually coba or nyoba. Boleh saya coba? asks to try clothes on or taste something, and coba before a verb softens a request: Coba lihat ini (Have a look at this).
Casually buka, and buka on its own means open for business: Tokonya buka jam berapa?
items.cultureNote: In Ramadan, buka puasa is breaking the fast at sunset. Friends and colleagues often do it together (bukber, buka bersama), and non-Muslims are welcome.

items.english: to close, to shut; to cover
items.registerNotes: Casually tutup: Tutup pintunya, ya. A sign saying tutup means closed.

items.english: to change, to replace; to pay back
items.registerNotes: Casually ganti: ganti baju (change clothes), ganti bus (change buses), Nanti saya ganti uangnya (I'll pay you back).
items.pitfallNote: Ganti is swapping one thing for another. When something changes by itself, it's berubah.

items.registerNotes: Casually jemput: Nanti aku jemput di stasiun (I'll pick you up at the station).
items.pitfallNote: Only for collecting a person. Picking up a thing is ambil: ambil paket, ambil tas.
items.cultureNote: Hosts and family often insist on picking you up from the airport or station; it's a way of making you welcome.

items.english: to take (someone somewhere), to drop off; to deliver
items.registerNotes: Casually antar, anter or nganterin: Aku anterin pulang, ya (I'll take you home). Delivery is antar too: layanan antar.
items.cultureNote: Hosts usually walk a departing guest to the door or the gate; seeing someone out properly is part of the visit.

items.registerNotes: Casually pesan, often said pesen or mesen: Mau pesan apa? For rooms and tickets too: Saya sudah pesan kamar.
items.pitfallNote: As a noun, pesan is a message: Ada pesan untuk saya? (Is there a message for me?)

items.registerNotes: Casually nabung: Aku lagi nabung buat liburan (I'm saving for a holiday).
items.pitfallNote: Only for money. Saving time is hemat waktu, and saving a file is menyimpan.

items.registerNotes: Something changes on its own: Jakarta sudah banyak berubah. Changing something yourself is mengubah (mengubah rencana, to change the plan); swapping one thing for another is ganti.
Permisi, mau tanya… (Excuse me, can I ask…) is the everyday polite opener. Casually tanya or nanya.
items.pitfallNote: Asking for something is minta, not bertanya: Boleh minta air? (Could I have some water?)

items.english: to invite (someone along), to ask someone to come
items.registerNotes: Casually ajak or ngajak: Dia ngajak saya makan (She asked me out for a meal).
items.cultureNote: Whoever does the inviting is generally expected to pay: yang ngajak, yang bayar, as people say.

items.english: to contact, to get in touch with
items.registerNotes: Polite and a little formal: Nanti saya hubungi (I'll be in touch). Casually people say kontak, chat or WA: Nanti aku WA, ya.
items.cultureNote: WhatsApp is how nearly everyone keeps in touch, from friends to landlords and small businesses, so nomor WA is the number to ask for.

items.english: to chat, to have a chat
items.registerNotes: Mostly heard as ngobrol, which is fine in all but formal settings: Kami ngobrol sampai malam (We chatted till late).
Casually nolak: Dia nolak tawarannya (He turned the offer down).
items.cultureNote: A blunt no can seem rude, so people turn things down softly: Lain kali, ya (Another time) or Maaf, belum bisa (Sorry, I can't just now).

items.registerNotes: Casually telepon or nelpon: Nanti aku telepon, ya. Most calls are made on WhatsApp.
